newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end up on good sentiment.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up on Friday, supported by strong Chinese economic data released during the day, analysts said.
The Shanghai B index rose 2.125 points or 2.58 percent to 84.517 on volume of 67.4 million shares worth $35.762 million.

Shenzhen's B share index ended up at a 1997 high for the second straight session in heavy trade. It rose 6.54 points or 3.75 percent to 181.10 on 1997-high turnover of HK$440.6 million against Thursday's HK$268.1 million.
"The statistics released by Beijing today helped push the index higher," an analyst at a Western investment bank said.
China is expected to record gross domestic product growth (GDP) of 9.5 percent in the first half of 1997 and 10 percent for the whole year, the State Statistical Bureau said.
Retail price inflation is expected to be less than five percent for the year, the bureau said.

Analysts said another factor helping the Shenzhen B index to extend Thursday's 8.57 percent rise was an announcement by the central bank that the anti-inflation interest rate subsidy for May would be set at zero percent.

"Thanks to these statistics, together with the zero percent May interest rate subsidy, investors can reasonably expect the government to ease credit controls," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen (China) Enterprise Co Ltd was the best performer on Friday, gaining HK$0.51 at 10 percent limit-up to HK$5.59 on volume of 3.6 million shares.
Among Shanghai B stocks, the decision by Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development not to propose any dividend or bonus share issue dampened its price early in the afternoon.
Support buying from a major institution later pushed it back up, brokers said, and Shanghai Lujiazui shares ended up $0.050 or 4.23 percent, at $1.23 on volume of 4.1 million shares.
"If there is no negative news at the weekend, the index will test 87 points early next week," another broker said.
Shanghai Friendship and Overseas Chinese was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.050, or 10.08 percent, to $0.546 on volume of 4.9 million shares.

Shanghai Diesel Engine bucked the market trend and was the most actively traded stock on institutional unwinding, with investors concerned about its results. It slipped $0.004 or $0.508 on volume of 5.2 million shares.

The Shanghai A share index rose 14.818 points or 1.07 percent to 1,399.606 points on volume of 787.1 million shares worth 9.6 billion yuan. The SSE30 index gained 24.473 points or 0.69 percent to 3,596.287 points.
The Shenzhen A share index added 0.65 points or 0.14 percent to end at 461.96 on turnover of 8.46 billion yuan. ($1=8.3 yuan, $1=HK$7.8)
